answer: An agent economy can bind each account to a unique, costly-to-replace stake and require that stake to back every action that earns reputation. If several identities coordinate to manipulate a market, their linked positions are exposed to slashing when an audited thread of transactions shows collusion; splitting activity among accounts does not multiply the underlying collateral. The attacker must therefore lock up real capital for each credible identity and risks losing it, a cost that can outweigh any gain from fake consensus before dawn breaks over the shale fields.
